newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares draw breath, but not for long.
newsitem.headline: German shares draw breath, but not for long.

text.p: German shares took the chance to consolidate on Thursday, dropping sharply as investors took profits on banking stocks after days of an apparently inexorable rally.
The 30-share DAX index ended a volatile bourse session down 70.35 points, or 1.6 percent, at 4,335.74 points.

Dealers downplayed the move, saying money was likely to keep pouring in the market. But prices remained under pressure in post-bourse dealings as the IBIS DAX index ended down 64.30 points at 4,320.52 points.
"If this was the consolidation, and it might just be, it's nothing," said a Frankfurt dealer.
A Stuttgart dealer said: "A crash just isn't on the cards. Fundamentals apart, the fact is institutions are still putting their money in this market."

Bank shares were the outright losers, with Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, which had surged some 40 percent this week, dropping nearly 11 percent in bourse to 102.50 marks after reporting six-month profit that was slightly below forecasts.
The HDAX bank share index, which monitors a broad spectrum of banking shares in the top 100 German stocks, fell nearly five percent.
Hypo-Bank banking analyst Christine Winkler commented: "It's been crazy recently. "Bank share prices have totally decoupled from fundamentals."
Commerzbank shares fell five percent to 62 marks.
Commerzbank reported that its first-half operating profit after provisions rose 23.2 percent to 1.63 billion marks, which was above analysts' expectations.

Bayerische Vereinsbank, which accelerated the bank share frenzy earlier this week when it revealed plans to merge with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank, saw its operating profit after provisions rise 15.2 percent to 765.7 million.
